name: Fergus

attributes.attribute: ancestral father of the British people

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fergus (Feargus) is an Irish hero name. In Irish tradition no name carries a stronger sense of virility. Male potency, or manhood, is what the name means. Some sources translate the meaning even as semen. Countless figures share the name. Ten of them are warriors of the Fianna. So many bearers exist that some scholars think Fergus was a title of kingship, not one man's name. Most bearers are minor figures. Most of them come from Ulster's northern province; they all may trace back to a single original. Fergus Fínbél was the Fianna's poet. He advised Fionn Mac Cumhaill; certain sources name Fionn his father. Fergus Foga ruled early in Ulster and invented the spear. A separate bearer, Fergus Lethderg, a son of the settler Nemed, fathered the line of the British people.

okr.objective: Fergus is an Irish hero name meaning male potency, borne by dozens of figures including ten warriors of the Fianna.
key_results: The name Fergus means male potency or manhood.
Ten bearers of the name belong to the Fianna band of warriors.
Fergus Fínbél was the Fianna's poet and an advisor to Fionn Mac Cumhaill.
Fergus Foga was an early Ulster king credited with inventing the spear.
